points: what you like to do together

questions.text: Describe a friend you have known for a long time.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe a friend you have known for a long time. You should say: who this person is; how you met; what you like to do together; and explain why your friendship has lasted so long.

questions.text: Do you think you will still be friends in ten years?
questions.say: Thank you. Do you think you will still be friends in ten years?

questions.text: What qualities make someone a good friend?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about a friend you have known for a long time, and I'd like to discuss with you some more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all friendship. What qualities make someone a good friend?

questions.text: Is it easier to make friends when you are a child or an adult?
questions.say: Is it easier to make friends when you are a child or an adult?

questions.text: Can you really be friends with someone you have only met online?
questions.say: Now let's talk about friendship and technology. Can you really be friends with someone you have only met online?

questions.text: Has social media made friendships stronger or weaker?
questions.say: Has social media made friendships stronger or weaker?

questions.text: Do people today have more friends than people did in the past?
questions.say: Do people today have more friends than people did in the past?
